To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) we develop a theory for the bit-rate needed for a given task and (2) we use this theory to design unsupervised training objectives for compressors that can achieve large bit-rate savings compared to JPEG.

(1) the bit-rate needed to preserve the performance of all invariant downstream tasks is proportional to the number of transformations that preserve the task's output, and (2) we train a generic neural image compressor that achieves more than 1000× compression compared to JPEG without loss in performance of a variety of downstream tasks.

(a) lossy compression is more effective than lossless compression for lossless prediction, and (b) a neural compressor trained to preserve the information required to solve a wide class of tasks is effective for a variety of predictive tasks.
